title: Complementary 3D STEM-EELS and APT Analysis for Chemical Composition Analysis of DRAM Contact Area
content: The combined analysis of TEM (Transmission Electron Microscopy) and APT (Atom Probe Tomography) for the same region of interest offers a complementary approach to understanding 3D (three-dimensional) structures and chemical compositions at the atomic scale [1]. The spatial resolution of TEM, which operates at the angstrom level, allows for precise identification of elemental positions and sample structures [2]. Meanwhile, APT provides high chemical sensitivity at the ppm (parts-per-million) level, enabling the detection of trace elements that may not be discernible through TEM-based compositional analysis. Additionally, TEM-EDS (Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy) can enhance APT data by distinguishing difficult to resolve elements due to APT's mass resolution limitations [3]. Integrating these analytical techniques improves the accuracy of mapping nanoscale elemental structures and chemical compositions within the same area.
